code.originalText: Five-week review: potassium and ECG on fluoxetine 60 mg, CBT-E progress, mood, and safety

text.paragraph: Five-week review: potassium and ECG on fluoxetine 60 mg, CBT-E progress, mood, and safety. [S]

Ms. Spencer returns four weeks after the consultation. She has had seven CBT-E sessions, twice a week, and keeps her self-monitoring record every day. Binge eating with vomiting has fallen to about three times a week, and she eats breakfast and lunch on four or five days a week. She took fluoxetine 20 mg for a week, 40 mg for a week, and has taken 60 mg each morning for two weeks. She had mild nausea in the first week, which passed; she sleeps well and has had no agitation or restlessness. The nurse's phone check ten days after the start found no concerns. She has taken potassium chloride twice daily. She has not booked a dental examination. Her mood is better and she has had no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1990-03-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 61.6 kg, BMI 19.4; lying blood pressure 106/66 and pulse 70, standing 104/68 and pulse 82 after three minutes
Parotid glands a little smaller; enamel erosion unchanged

Bulimia nervosa, severe: recurrent binge eating, each time with self-induced vomiting, averaging about ten episodes a week for about three years, hidden from everyone; self-worth tied closely to body shape and weight; no laxatives, diuretics, diet pills, or excessive exercise. SCOFF 4 of 5; EDE-Q global score 3.9. Findings: bilateral parotid enlargement, enamel erosion on the inner surfaces of the upper front teeth, calluses on the backs of two knuckles of the right hand, a pulse rise of 22 per minute on standing, low potassium and chloride with a raised bicarbonate, and a raised amylase; BMI 19.3. Synthetic modern episode linked to her own public account of bulimia
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis by DSM-5-TR criteria; severity is graded by the average number of compensatory episodes a week (8 to 13 is severe).
Hypokalemia (potassium 3.1 mmol/L) with low chloride and metabolic alkalosis from repeated vomiting; QTc 452 ms; no palpitations, weakness, or fainting
S — Synthetic presenting laboratory finding; resolved when potassium was normal on two checks.

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate: about two months of low mood, tiredness, poor sleep, and feeling worthless and hopeless, with little pleasure in things she used to enjoy; PHQ-9 14 with item 9 scored 0; an earlier episode of depression after childbirth. Synthetic modern episode linked to her own public account of depression
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the earlier episode is the post-natal depression she described publicly.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Eating Disorders, Fourth Edition (2023); Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026)

Follow-up: CBT-E weekly. Book a dental examination. Preventive visit in four weeks. Three-month review in eight weeks with electrolytes, the EDE-Q, and the PHQ-9. Next scheduled visit 1990-04-13: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
